body: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is Capcom's Nintendo DS puzzle adventure about Sissel, a ghost who has lost the memory of his life and death. Over a single night he follows a chain of people in danger, using supernatural powers to discover what connects them. Directed and written by Shu Takumi, it turns a murder mystery into a sequence of physical interventions. Sissel cannot simply question everyone or walk through the city. He has to understand the objects around him well enough to make the living world respond.

In the Ghost World, time stops and Sissel can move between the cores of nearby objects. Returning to the real world lets him perform a trick with the object he possesses, such as shifting something into another character's path. That action may create access to a new core or change what somebody does next. A room is consequently both a collection of mechanisms and a route through space. The player has to consider what an object can do before deciding whether its position can lead somewhere useful.

Sissel can return to the four minutes before a person's death and try to prevent it. Repeated observation reveals the sequence of movements that produces the fatal result, allowing a small intervention to redirect it. Failure becomes information for another attempt rather than the end of the investigation. The expressive animation makes those sequences readable and gives the characters a strong physical personality. Ghost Trick builds its mystery through consequences: changing the position of one ordinary thing can save a life and uncover another part of the night's larger explanation.
